questions.knowledge_point: Comparing an Exponential Function and a Logarithmic Function
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the first term as

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡(x){e}^{-2x}=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{e}^{2x}}.
$$

Both the numerator and denominator approach $\infty $ as $x\to \infty .$ However, since ${e}^{2x}≫\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)$ for large values of $x,$ the denominator is growing much faster than the numerator. Consequently, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{e}^{2x}}=0.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x){e}^{-2x}+3) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{e}^{2x}}+3) \\  & =0+3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8x)}=\infty 
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }(\frac{{x}^{5}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8x)}+6)=\infty 
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Comparing the Relative Magnitude of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the limit as

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2x-3}.
$$

The numerator here is a bounded, oscillating function with

$$
|-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x|\le 5.
$$

However, the denominator $2x-3$ grows without bound as $x\to \infty .$ So the denominator is growing much faster than the numerator, and we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x}={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2x-3}=0.
$$

We can see this from the graph of $y=\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3-2x},$ shown below:

questions.knowledge_point: Comparing the Relative Magnitude of a Trigonometric Function
questions.worked_solution:
The numerator here is a bounded, oscillating function with 

$$
|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|\le 1.
$$

However, the denominator $x$ grows without bound as $x\to \infty .$ Since the denominator grows much faster than the (bounded) numerator, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x}=0.
$$

We can see this from the graph of $y=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{x},$ shown below:
